title: Rehearsal Matrix and Staggered Canary Ladder — Apr 2025 (scratch)
body:
Purpose:
This scratch doc captures a compact rehearsal matrix (who does what during a rehearsal), a staggered canary ladder plan tuned for low-latency inference services, and a short template for the release notes + postmortem outline. Intended as the working runbook for the next small-scope release (feature set: response-caching-hotfix + kernel-selection-tune).

Context / constraints:
- Target: low-risk night micro-window (UTC 02:00–05:00) to minimize traffic.
- Services: inference-router, kv-cache, runtime-worker, telemetry-ingest. All three services must pass smoke before traffic shift.
- SLA: keep 99th p90 latency within 1.2x baseline.
- Fallback model: auto-route to model-v1-quantized if latency spike > threshold.

Quick summary timeline (high-level):
- T-72h: Finalize rehearsal matrix, invite cross-team attendants, lock smoke-test scripts.
- T-24h: Dry-run in staging with synthetic traffic, validate canary-weight schedule.
- T-6h: Preflight meeting, signoff from SRE, infra, and product.
- T-0: Start canary ladder. Increment weights with 10–20 minute plateaus.
- T+120m: If no regressions, full cutover; else execute step-down.

Rehearsal matrix (roles + responsibilities):
- Release Conductor (Aisha): start runbook, maintain timeline, trigger notifications, decide go/no-go.
- SRE Lead (Daniel): validate infra scaling, watch latency/availability dashboards, run roll-back steps.
- Runtime Owner (Mariana): observe model-serving metrics (token throughput, OOMs), manage runtime patches.
- Telemetry Owner (Ethan): ensure observability pipelines are healthy, check sampling, ensure logs are flowing.
- QA Runner: execute smoke and canary validation scripts (see smoke checklist).
- Customer Success on-call: prep comms templates for customers if degradation > severity-2.

Rehearsal checklist (T-72h → T-6h):
- [ ] Confirm capacity reservations for Dedicated pools for the night window (infra ticket JIRA-RELAY-1423).
- [ ] Lock the exact model versions and quantization profiles in release config.
- [ ] Publish draft release notes (internal-facing) + consumer-facing microcopy.
- [ ] Verify rollback artifact and test revert in staging once.
- [ ] Validate canary traffic shaping infra (rate-limiter + router rules).
- [ ] Prepare emergency throttle curve and safety-lane numeric thresholds.
- [ ] Cross-check runbook contact roster and escalation ladder.

Smoke-test quick catalog (scripts referenced by name):
- smoke-inference-basic.sh: 100 short prompts (mean length 16 tokens), assert p95 < 1.2x baseline and no errors.
- smoke-kv-cache-hitrate.py: ensure cache hit rate > 60% for representative prefix set.
- smoke-memory-guard.py: run for 15m to ensure no steady memory growth > 20MB/min per worker.
- smoke-telemetry-integrity.sh: assert no >5% sample drop and pipeline lag < 60s.

Staggered canary ladder (recommended cadence and guardrails):
- Start: route 0.5% of global requests to canary (duration 10m). Quick health check.
- Step 1: 2% (duration 15m). Verify token cost, p95, error rate.
- Step 2: 8% (duration 20m). Run full smoke suite.
- Step 3: 25% (duration 30m). Look for latency tail changes, KV cache regressions.
- Step 4: 60% (duration 30m). Last validation window.
- Cutover: 100% if all pass.

Immediate stop conditions (any triggers -> abort/invoke rollback):
- latency_p95 > 1.4x baseline for 3 consecutive intervals,
- error rate increase > 0.5% absolute or >4x baseline,
- memory growth sustained beyond guard threshold,
- telemetry ingestion lag > 5 minutes,
- unexpected increase in unit token cost > 20% (cost guard).

Rollforward vs rollback decision notes:
- Prefer rollforward patch if root cause is quickly addressable with stateless change (config toggle, kernel revert).
- Rollback (revert traffic entirely to stable) if service-level error or client-visible regression persists after 2 consecutive plateau checks.

Operator play actions (short commands & pointers):
- Pause canary: PUT /router/canary/weight {0} (auth: release-key).
- Revert to previous model: update serving-routing to model-v1-quantized via infra console (runbook step 7).
- Throttle: apply token_bucket throttle on /generate endpoint to 70% baseline.

Stakeholder comm microcopy (for Slack + Email):
- Internal short: "Rolling a small canary for runtime kernel tune. Monitoring latency and errors. SRE on watch — we'll post updates at each plateau."
- Customer-facing (if visible): "We're deploying an efficiency update to inference serving that should reduce tail latency. If you see any change in responses, please contact support@redwood.ai with subject 'Inference latency'."

Release notes fragments (consumer-facing drafts):
- Feature: Reduced inference tail latency for short prompts via kernel selection refinements.
- Fix: Prevent rare memory drift in runtime-worker during heavy long-sequence workloads.
- Note: No model weight changes — responses are functionally identical to previous release.

Post-release validation plan (T+0 → T+72h):
- Hourly first 12h: automated health checks + p95/p99 telemetry snapshot.
- Daily: compare quality evals on a canonical prompt set for regression drift.
- T+48h: cost delta assessment (tokens/unit cost) and traffic pattern analysis.
- T+72h: final signoff and move release-ticket to DONE.

Light postmortem outline (to copy into GH issue / Confluence):
- Summary: one-liner describing what shipped and outcome.
- Timeline: annotated timestamps for key events (deploy start, guardrail hits, mitigation).
- Impact: user-visible symptoms, metrics and affected customers.
- Root cause: technical explanation.
- Corrective actions: short-term and long-term (owners + ETA).
- Follow-ups: tickets for observability, test coverage, docs.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Should we tighten initial canary plateau from 10m -> 20m for inference routes to catch slow ramp regressions? tradeoff vs time-to-full.
- Add synthetic latency-injection test in staging to better exercise fallback path.
- Push a small update to the release-notes microcopy to call out cost-safety guard for enterprise customers.

Appendix: links / immediate references
- Staging smoke script dir: github.com/redwood-inference/release-scripts/tree/main/staging-smoke
- Dashboard: dashboards.redwood.internal/d/latency/inference-runtime
- Pager channel: #ops-release-watch
- Revert artifact location: s3://releases/redwood/rollback-artifacts/2025-04-02

Notes: this is intentionally compact and conversational — use as the live rehearsal document, edit during the dry-run.
